title: Grouping with $group
idea: `$group` merges documents that share the same key into one output document. You set the key in `_id` and compute every other field from the group.

analogy.text: Sorting a drawer of receipts into one envelope per month, then writing a total on each envelope.
analogy.breaks: Envelopes keep the receipts; a group keeps only its key and totals.

points: `_id` is the group key. `'$city'` means: use each document's `city`.
`_id: null` puts every document in one group, for a grand total.
Use an object as `_id` to group by several fields at once.

hero.title: Orders fall into groups by city

steps.caption: `$group` receives every order. The key `'$city'` decides which group each one joins.
Order 1 creates the Lisbon group. Order 2 creates the Porto group.
Orders with a known city join its group. No new group appears.
Order 7 brings a new city, so a Faro group appears.
Each group collapses into one document. `$sum` added up the `total` of every order inside it.
`$sort` on `_id` puts the documents in a fixed order. Group output alone has none.

code.title: Three ways to choose the key
code.caption: Same data as every page in this chapter. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: Group by `city`: `'$city'` reads each order's city. `$sum` adds up `total`.
Group output has no promised order, so sort on `_id`, the key.
`_id: null` gives every document the same key: one group, a grand total.
The key can be an object: here two fields, `city` and `status`.
One group per distinct pair. The same city with another status is a new group.
Dot notation sorts on fields inside the key object.

pitfalls: `_id: 'city'` without the `$` groups every document under the text 'city'.
After `$group`, only `_id` and your accumulator fields remain; other fields are gone.
Every non-`_id` field needs an accumulator: `{ x: '$total' }` raises an error.

quiz.why: No `$match`, so every status forms a group. Sorted by `_id`: cancelled, paid, pending.

takeaway: `$group` makes one document per `_id` value; accumulators fill the rest.
